Chippewas of Georgina Island

The Chippewas of Georgina Island identify themselves as an Anishinaabe Nation connected to Lake Simcoe. Their public account distinguishes their community history from the related Beausoleil and Rama communities; a separate case study introduces dated climate-adaptation planning.

01

The Nation’s own historical account

The Chippewas of Georgina Island’s public account follows Chief Joseph Snake’s community through the Coldwater experiment and a return to the Lake Simcoe islands. It distinguishes this history from those of the related communities under Chiefs Assance and Yellowhead. The Nation also describes continuing responsibilities toward water and future generations. Its legal and governance statements should be read as attributed institutional positions, not conclusions supplied by this directory.

Read the sources [1] Chippewas of Georgina Island First Nation

02

Climate planning with community knowledge

A national climate-assessment case study describes Georgina Island’s 2012–2015 adaptation project. It explains how community meetings, surveys and scientific information informed assessments of changing ice, water and other conditions. The account reports a planning process and proposed next steps. It expressly leaves later implementation progress unresolved, so it cannot establish present safety, ecological conditions or completed outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Canada in a Changing Climate / National Assessment Process
